Photograph: Oleksandr Ratushniak/Reuters Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Pressure stays on Russian economy until war is over, says Bessent US treasury secretary speaks with Russian counterpart who is controversially attending G20 talks; India’s Modi says war must end. What we know on day 1,651 Warren Murray with Guardian writers and agencies Mon 31 Aug 2026 21.03 EDT Last modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 22.33 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google No economic relief for Russia is ‌possible ‌until its war in Ukraine ‌ends, the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, has told a Russian counterpart. Bessent met with Anton Siluanov, the Russian finance minister, at a G20 finance ​leaders’ meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, where Moscow’s representatives were a surprise and unwelcome presence. A source told Reuters that Bessent said no agreements of any kind were ‌possible ‌until the war ended. The Russian finance minister’s ⁠first in-person G20 appearance ​since Russia ​invaded Ukraine ​has irritated ​European officials ‌who are ​working ​on more sanctions against Russia . Britain on Monday ramped up pressure on ⁠shadow financial systems underpinning Russia’s war economy, doubling penalties for sanctions breaches, the UK treasury said. Fines would increase from 50% of the value of a sanctions breach to 100%, said John ⁠Healey, the UK finance minister. The UK’s National Crime Agency issued a nationwide ‌alert targeting the Kremlin-backed A7 network, which the British government has said was used to route funds and evade restrictions. Four people ⁠were killed and more than ​a dozen injured in Russian air attacks on the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv and the surrounding region on Tuesday , local authorities said, as a sixth day of strikes began. In Kyiv, three people were killed ⁠and another five wounded, and a fire broke out in a non-residential area. In ‌Boryspil in the wider Kyiv ‌region, one person was killed and another nine, including a child, were injured after missiles and drones ‌damaged an apartment building and a business, said the governor, Tymur Tkachenko. Odesa in Ukraine’s south came under heavy attack on Monday night , including by glide bombs, local officials said. Kyiv suffers hours of daytime air raids as Russia deploys new jet-powered drones Read more It comes as Kyiv endures hours of daytime air raids and air raid warnings , Dan Sabbagh writes from the Ukrainian capital . Russia fired 800 jet-powered drones into Ukraine in the previous four days. Past versions of the Iranian-style Shahed drones were propeller-driven. In response, Ukrainian engineers are racing to make faster interceptor drones. “Four companies have developed the relevant interceptor drones, and one company has the most successful technology,” said Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukraine’s president. Nato ⁠fighter planes were scrambled, Latvia’s military said early on Tuesday, after ⁠a ​warning ‌of a ‌possible air ‌threat near the town of Ludza, close ‌to the Russian border. Separately, Russia’s ​north-western Leningrad region issued a drone ⁠threat alert, according ​to the governor, ‌Alexander ​Drozdenko. More than a dozen drones heading for Moscow were shot down, claimed the mayor, Sergei Sobyanin, on Tuesday morning. Ukrainian drones also caused damage in the Samara region, home to ⁠a number of major oil refineries about 800km (500 miles) south-east of Moscow, the local governor said. ​Finland restricted air ‌and maritime traffic close ​to Russia, armed ​forces of both countries said, as Russia’s north-western Leningrad region, home to major export ports, came under drone attack . Ukrainian drones have hit another Wildberries warehouse, this time in Ekaterinburg, Russia. The Russian local governor confirmed the strike ‌on Monday, claiming that drones ‌and debris ‌also struck residential buildings. There were ​no casualties, ​he said. The suspected Russian “shadow fleet” oil tanker MV Sun was boarded ⁠by the ⁠European Union’s ​naval mission in the Mediterranean on Sunday , said Kaja Kallas, the EU’s ⁠foreign policy chief. “The oil ‌tanker MV Sun, suspected ‌of sailing under false flag in breach of international maritime law, was boarded on August 30 in the ‌Mediterranean by Operation Eunavfor Med Irini forces for ​flag verification,” Kallas posted. The war in Ukraine must end for humanity’s sake, India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, ​told Vladimir Putin as the two met in Kyrgyzstan. “Every day that the war continues, humanity is, in effect, set back ​a step, whilst every step towards peace gives all of humanity real hope for peace,” Modi said. “We need to move from endless war to an end to the war, to a cessation of hostilities. And we will need to move precisely in this direction.” Despite international condemnation and sanctions, India, along with China, has remained one of the biggest buyers ‌of Russian oil , which has helped Moscow fund its war against Ukraine. Modi and the Russian president met on the sidelines of ‌the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit where Putin ⁠and his Chinese ​counterpart, Xi ⁠Jinping, also met and briefly discussed ⁠the ​Ukraine war, the ​Kremlin ​said. Indonesia said it was investigating claims that several citizens had joined the Russian military to fight in the war in Ukraine. Information from Ukrainian authorities was being checked, the foreign ministry in Jakarta said. It did not say how many Indonesians were under suspicion, but they risk losing their citizenship. “If the involvement of Indonesian citizens in the armed forces of a foreign country is verified, it is an individual act and does not represent the policy or position of the Indonesian government,” the foreign ministry said. ‘Everything’s smashed to bits’: Ukrainians turn anger on those storing weapons near their villages Read more Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that he ⁠held a “detailed ⁠and ​constructive” call with US envoys ⁠Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Both sides were ⁠working to finalise dates for ​their visit ‌to Ukraine. “I ‌also informed them about the situation on the battlefield, where Russia’s gains have been sparse and at the cost of ‌huge losses, and about the strikes,” Zelenskyy said. “We shall see what the US president’s representatives manage to achieve. September ⁠could bring about a lot ​of ​changes. And we, together ​with our partners, must ​do ‌everything we ​can ​to protect people.” Polish prosecutors are investigating a fire at a drone factory as an act of terrorism arranged by a foreign intelligence service. The fire at the WB Electronics factory in the central city of Skarzysko-Kamienna was started deliberately using a “device containing flammable materials”, a prosecution statement said. Several countries in eastern Europe have said they have been the target of spying and sabotage as part of a “hybrid war” by Russia. Ukraine’s top sanctions official, Vladyslav Vlasiuk, will visit Washington this week to urge members of the US House ⁠of Representatives to approve sweeping ⁠Russia sanctions legislation. It would enable the president to sanction Russian officials and authorise tariffs on China, India and other countries for buying Russian oil ​and gas. Some US lawmakers and industries are wary, though, that Donald Trump might abuse the powers that the legislation contains. The House ​has not yet scheduled a vote on the legislation. The agreement covers the supply of electricity from a photovoltaic plant of an approximately 12 MW capacity located in the Mikro Perivolaki area in Velestino, in the Prefecture of Magnesia. Coca-Cola Tria Epsilon will offtake 100% of the electricity generated by the project, which is estimated at approximately 16.5 GWh annually. As part of its parent company Coca-Cola HBC’s commitment to achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2040, Coca-Cola Tria Epsilon already sources 100% of the electricity used at its production facilities from renewable energy sources. Through this agreement, Coca-Cola Tria Epsilon will secure the supply of a “higher quality” green energy, while also supporting the development of new renewable energy projects in pursuit of a more sustainable future for all. METLEN has a strong and long-standing presence in the Greek and international renewable energy markets, with a proven track record in the development, construction (EPC), operation and maintenance (O&M) of large-scale energy projects. In Greece, METLEN has an operating renewable energy portfolio of approximately 0.5 GW in total capacity, while globally it has completed or is currently executing projects with a total capacity of 11.4 GW, across five continents. At the same time, METLEN’s Renewable Energy Aggregator, under the Company’s Integrated Utility platform, undertakes the full management and commercialisation of the electricity generated, ensuring its efficient integration into electricity markets. It represents a renewable energy portfolio with a total installed capacity of more than 2.2 GW across Greece, Italy and Romania. Corporate PPAs are a key pillar of METLEN’s strategy to provide integrated and competitive energy solutions to major industrial and commercial consumers. Through agreements such as this one with Coca-Cola Tria Epsilon, METLEN continues to play a leading role in shaping the evolving energy market and in accelerating Greece’s green transition.
